tasks.question: In general, do people prefer city life or country life?

cues.cue: people / prefer / city life for its opportunities
models: In general, people prefer city life for its opportunities, and this pattern is explained by better jobs and services, so cities keep attracting newcomers.

cues.cue: older generations / favour / the countryside
models: There is a tendency for older generations to favour the countryside, which suggests that peace and quiet matter more with age, and therefore rural areas remain popular among retirees.

cues.cue: young professionals / choose / cities for career growth
models: By and large, young professionals choose cities for career growth, and this tends to be the case because opportunities are more concentrated there, so migration to cities continues.

cues.cue: families / lean / towards quieter, greener areas
models: Generally speaking, families lean towards quieter, greener areas, although there are exceptions when good schools are only available in cities.

cues.cue: most people / value / convenience over space
models: As a rule, most people value convenience over space, and this is because busy lifestyles leave little time for long commutes, which suggests city living will remain the norm.

cues.cue: surveys / show / a slight preference for cities
models: It is commonly believed that most people prefer cities, although the evidence suggests opinion is far more evenly split than assumed.

tasks.question: On the whole, how do young people in your country spend their free time?

cues.cue: young people / get / news online
models: Generally speaking, young people get their news online, although there are exceptions when older family members still rely on television.

cues.cue: teenagers / spend / hours on social media
models: There is a tendency for teenagers to spend hours on social media, which suggests that screens dominate their free time, and therefore outdoor activities have declined.

cues.cue: young people / gather / with friends at weekends
models: On the whole, young people gather with friends at weekends, and this is consistent with the strong value placed on socialising at that age.

cues.cue: students / dedicate / free time to gaming
models: In most cases, students dedicate their free time to gaming, and this is largely due to the accessibility of consoles and phones, which means screens dominate leisure time.

cues.cue: many teenagers / play / sport regularly
models: As a rule, many teenagers play sport regularly, and this is because schools encourage physical activity, which suggests healthy habits are still common.

cues.cue: free time / revolve / increasingly around streaming platforms
models: Broadly speaking, free time revolves increasingly around streaming platforms, and this reflects the fact that entertainment is now available on demand, since traditional TV schedules matter less.

tasks.question: Broadly speaking, how important is technology in people's daily lives?

cues.cue: technology / plays / a central role in daily routines
models: Broadly speaking, technology plays a central role in daily routines, and this reflects the fact that most tasks now depend on a device, since even simple errands rely on apps.

cues.cue: people / rely / heavily on their phones
models: On the whole, people rely heavily on their phones, and this is consistent with how deeply connected daily life has become, because even basic tasks depend on them.

cues.cue: most households / depend / on smart devices
models: In most cases, households depend on smart devices for everyday tasks, and this is largely due to the convenience they offer, which means fewer manual chores remain.

cues.cue: technology / shapes / how people work and socialise
models: In general, technology shapes how people work and socialise, and this pattern is explained by its presence in nearly every aspect of modern life, so its influence keeps growing.

cues.cue: some people / manage / to limit their screen use
models: Generally speaking, technology dominates daily life, although there are exceptions when people deliberately limit their screen use.

cues.cue: younger generations / consider / technology essential
models: As a rule, younger generations consider technology essential, and this is because they have never known life without it, which suggests reliance will only deepen further.

tasks.question: In most cases, why do people decide to learn English?

cues.cue: students / study / English to travel more easily

cues.cue: many learners / choose / English for higher education

cues.cue: workers / need / English for international companies

cues.cue: young people / learn / English through entertainment and media

cues.cue: most reasons / connect / to broader career prospects

tasks.question: Generally, how healthy are people's lifestyles these days?

cues.cue: modern lifestyles / involve / far less physical activity
models: In general, modern lifestyles involve far less physical activity, and this pattern is explained by desk jobs and screen-based leisure, so overall fitness levels have declined.

cues.cue: people / eat / more processed food than before
models: There is a tendency for people to eat more processed food than before, which suggests that convenience often outweighs nutrition, and therefore diet-related health problems are rising.

cues.cue: many adults / struggle / to get enough sleep
models: More often than not, many adults struggle to get enough sleep, and the main reason for this is demanding work schedules, which affects overall wellbeing.

cues.cue: younger people / show / growing interest in fitness
models: Generally speaking, lifestyles have become less active, although there are exceptions when younger people show a growing interest in fitness.

cues.cue: most households / consume / more sugar than recommended
models: As a rule, most households consume more sugar than recommended, and this is because sweetened products are heavily marketed, which suggests dietary habits need improvement.

cues.cue: health experts / consider / current habits concerning
models: It is commonly believed that health experts consider current habits concerning, although the evidence suggests small improvements are gradually taking place.

tasks.question: On the whole, how do most students prepare for their exams?

cues.cue: students / rely / on last-minute revision
models: On the whole, students rely on last-minute revision, and this is consistent with the pressure many feel to cover material quickly before deadlines.

cues.cue: learners / use / online resources to study
models: In general, learners use online resources to study, and this pattern is explained by the convenience and range of material available, so textbooks are used less often.

cues.cue: many students / form / study groups before exams
models: There is a tendency for students to form study groups before exams, which suggests that peer support helps with motivation, and therefore group revision remains common.

cues.cue: students / practise / with past papers
models: More often than not, students practise with past papers, and the main reason for this is that it helps them understand the exam format, which builds confidence.

cues.cue: some students / start / preparing weeks in advance
models: Generally speaking, most students prepare shortly before exams, although there are exceptions when some start weeks in advance.

cues.cue: exam preparation / depend / heavily on time management
models: As a rule, exam preparation depends heavily on time management, and this is because poor planning leads to rushed revision, which suggests organisation is key to success.
